newsitem.title: USA: Ford increases production of Expeditions.
newsitem.headline: Ford increases production of Expeditions.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Tuesday it increased production capacity for its Expedition sport utility vehicle by about seven percent, a move that will allow it to make up output lost during a seat supplier strike by the end of May.
The line-rate increase from 42 Expeditions an hour to 45 will allow Ford's Wayne, Mich., truck plant to produce an additional 17,000 vehicles annually.

Ford also said it has completed the installation of seats into 20,000 Expeditions and Econoline vans that were built without seats during the 24-day February strike at Johnson Controls Inc seat plants in Plymouth, Mich. and Oberlin, Ohio.
The seatless trucks were completed at a vacant plant in Brighton, Mich., rented from Cars and Concepts Inc., while Ford continued to make Expeditions with seats in Wayne.
Ford said the Wayne truck plant begin production of the new Lincoln Navigator sport utility vehicle, based on the Expedition's platform, in mid-May.

By mid-April, Ford said its Lorain, Ohio, truck line will have made up all of the production lost during the strike. On March 16, Ford completed installation of seats into Econoline vans and Club Wagons built without them.
